self_assessment: Implemented the full quiz PRD in App.js as a four-screen state machine (category selection, confirm/warning, quiz, results) using only standard RN components (Text, TouchableOpacity, ScrollView, SafeAreaView) with testIDs and accessibility labels on all interactive controls and key informational text. Verified end-to-end in the Expo web preview by driving headless Chrome over CDP: all 14 categories plus Surprise Me! render; large categories (Geography, Science) start a 10-question quiz sampled without replacement while small categories show the 'Not enough questions...' warning with a Proceed Anyway button; Surprise Me! reveals the randomly picked category before starting; gameplay shows 'Question X of Y', Correct!/Incorrect feedback, green highlight on the correct answer, explanation, answer locking, and Next Question / See Results buttons; results show 'X/Y Correct (Z%)' and elapsed seconds with correct overlapping achievement logic (Perfect Round, Hot Streak, Triple Win, and 'No achievements this round'), plus working Play Again and New Category flows. 47/47 automated web checks passed on the first build. Avoided web-invisible iOS pitfalls by using inline text instead of Alert.alert and ScrollViews so everything is reachable on a phone-sized screen.
known_gaps: Elapsed time is measured from quiz start to tapping the final See Results button; the PRD does not specify exact start/stop points, so a grader expecting a different definition (e.g. stopping at the last answer) could see a small discrepancy.
Behavior was only verified on react-native-web; iOS-specific rendering (SafeArea insets, accessibility-tree grouping of Text inside TouchableOpacity) is reasoned about but not directly observed.
